name: Meridian Appliances Ltd
about: A fictional kitchen-appliance maker, used to show the research view without live data.

flags.text: Only 65% of the last five years' profit showed up as operating cash.
Free cash flow (estimated) was negative in 4 of the last 5 years.
Working-capital cycle stretched from 72 to 92 days.

items.quote: We remain confident of 15 to 18% revenue growth for FY27, led by the built-in category.
items.speaker: CFO

items.quote: We should exit FY26 at a 14% EBITDA margin as the new plant stabilises.
items.speaker: MD

items.quote: For the full year FY26, we are guiding to mid-teens growth.
items.speaker: MD

items.quote: The Sanand plant will be commissioned by Q3 FY27, taking capacity to 2.4 million units.
items.speaker: MD
items.why: Plant is due Q3 FY27; Q2 FY27 is the latest reported quarter.

items.quote: Working capital should come back to around 70 days by year-end.
items.speaker: CFO
items.why: Working-capital days were 92 at FY26 year-end against ~70 promised.

synthesis.one_line: Growth is real and ahead of guidance, but it is being bought with working capital: profit is not turning into cash.

business.summary: Designs and manufactures kitchen appliances — hobs, chimneys and built-in ovens — sold through dealers and modern retail in India.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Management calls FY26 'a year of cash discipline'.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Cash from operations was 67% of profit in FY26; working-capital days rose to 92.
Revenue grew 18% in FY26 and 16% in H1 FY27, consistent with mix commentary.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Margins to expand as the new plant stabilises.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Operating margin has held at 12–13% for eight quarters; no expansion yet.

guidance_now.what: Sanand plant by Q3 FY27, 2.4 mn units

bull.point: Revenue compounding at 14% a year for five years with steady 12–13% margins.
H1 FY27 growth of 16% is inside the 15–18% guided range.
New capacity adds headroom just as built-in demand is growing.

bear.point: 65% cash conversion over five years: growth is being funded by receivables and inventory.
Free cash flow (est.) negative in four of the last five years; borrowings up 2.5× since FY21.
Two margin and working-capital promises missed in the last year.
